raw_response:
I will keep my land in a simple pattern that I know well and can manage at my age. I have 16.1 mu, well irrigation, and some family labor is away working, so I will not make the plan too complicated. I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is my main cropping system and it gives me steady grain for the household and cash income. I will keep a smaller part in cotton because I already grow it and I want to spread risk instead of putting everything into grain. I will use better seed on all three crops because I care more about stable yield than saving a little on seed. I will fertilize wheat and maize a bit more heavily than cotton because they are the backbone of my farm. Since I have access to well water, I will irrigate at the key times rather than depend only on rainfall. I will also keep tillage practical and familiar, mostly rotary tillage for the grain land and ploughing for cotton ground. Because I am 67 and labor is limited, I will not push for the highest possible input level; I will aim for stable management, controlled costs, and reliable yields.
